packageRules.description: One weekly PR for all non-major updates, so CI runs once
Keep GitHub Actions bumps in their own weekly PR

prBodyTemplate:
## What issue does this solve?

Keep the repository's dependencies current. Review the exact proposed versions below; an update is not proof that an existing bug or vulnerability is fixed.

## Example of the problem

The current package and workflow declarations use the older versions listed below. Check that related package-manager declarations stay consistent before merging.

## Proposal and solution

Apply the generated dependency changes and lockfile updates together, then run the repository's required checks and review loop.

## Why this is better

This groups dependency maintenance into a reviewable change. Compatibility still needs verification; no speed, security, or accuracy improvement is claimed without evidence.

## Before and after

The generated change list provides the current and proposed versions:

{{{table}}}

## Evidence and results

Version declarations are the observed before/after evidence. Runtime or performance comparisons have not been run by this description generator. Read current-head CI and raw logs before merging; authors must add concrete fix and test evidence when resolving findings.

{{{warnings}}}
{{{notes}}}

## How to use it in everyday work

After merge, install the reviewed lockfile with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and run the normal repository checks. Keep docs and configuration in sync. Publishing and deployment remain separately authorized.

{{{controls}}}
{{{footer}}}
